newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar threatens to cut links with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Qatar threatens to cut links with Israel.

text.p: Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem, said on Wednesday that Arab states should sever links with Israel to force the Jewish state to move forward on the peace process with the Palestinians.
Jordan and Egypt have signed peace deals with Israel.

"Israel must understand all its relations with the Arab and outside world are directly connected to the peace process and the situation in Jerusalem," Husseini told Reuters during a visit to Qatar for a week-long exhibition on Jerusalem,.
"I believe that all Arab states must cut their relations to force Israel to honour its commitments under the peace process," he said.
Qatar also hinted it might sever trade links with Israel if the Jewish state continued to build Jewish settlements in Arab East Jerusalem and violate peace deals with Palestinians.

Asked if Qatar was prepared to break ties with Israel if current Israeli-Palestinian clashes in the West Bank sparked by the building drive continued, Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani told reporters:
"Everything is possible if the Israeli leadership continues to disregard its international commitments and expand Jewish settlements."
Qatar and Oman have raced ahead of other Gulf Arab states to set up economic relations with Israel since the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestinians in 1993.
But they stopped short of establishing diplomatic ties pending an overall settlement of the Arab-Israeli conflict.
Israel has trade missions in the two countries and Oman has opened a trade representative office in Tel Aviv.
Oman said on Sunday it had frozen ties with Israel over the settlements policy.

Israeli-Palestinian clashes broke out after right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers eight days ago to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a new Jewish settlement in territory occupied by Israel.
Qatar in December froze ties with Israel over its failure to implement peace deals with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
